arxiv-2106-10952.title: Spliced Binned-Pareto Distribution for robust modeling of heavy-tailed time series
arxiv-2106-10952.creator: Elena Ehrlich AWS ProServeMiami, FL, USA eeehrlic@amazon.com Laurent CallotAmazon ResearchSeattle, WA, USA lcallot@amazon.com, François-Xavier Aubet Amazon ResearchVienna, Austria aubetf@amazon.com
arxiv-2106-10952.description: Abstract This work proposes a novel method to robustly and accurately model time series with heavy-tailed noise, in non-stationary scenarios. In many practical application time series have heavy-tailed noise that significantly impacts the performance of classical forecasting models; in particular, accurately modeling a distribution over extreme events is crucial to performing accurate time series anomaly detection.

arxiv-2204-13758.title: Using edt0l systems to solve some equations in the solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups
arxiv-2204-13758.creator: Andrew Duncan, Alex Evetts, Derek F. Holt, Sarah Rees
arxiv-2204-13758.description: Abstract We investigate the solution sets to equations in the solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups B ​ S ​ ( 1 , k ) BS(1,k) , k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 , and show that these sets are represented by edt0l languages in some cases.

arxiv-2206-05247.title: Quantum networks boosted by entanglement with a control system
arxiv-2206-05247.creator: Tamal Guha, Saptarshi Roy, Giulio Chiribella
arxiv-2206-05247.description: Abstract Networks of quantum devices with coherent control over their configuration offer promising advantages in quantum information processing. So far, the investigation of these advantages assumed that the control system was initially uncorrelated with the data processed by the network.

arxiv-2401-06795.title: AI and Generative AI for Research Discovery and Summarization Thanks: Department of Statistics, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA, 02138
arxiv-2401-06795.creator: Mark E. Glickman, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2401-06795.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mark E. Glickman, Yi Zhang. AI and generative AI tools, including chatbots like ChatGPT that rely on large language models (LLMs), have burst onto the scene this year, creating incredible opportunities to increase work productivity and improve our lives. Statisticians and data scientists have begun experiencing the benefits from the availability of these tools in numerous ways, such as the generation of programming code from text prompts to analyze data or fit statistical models.

arxiv-2407-01640.title: BADM: Batch ADMM for Deep Learning
arxiv-2407-01640.creator: Ouya Wang, Shenglong Zhou, and Geoffrey Ye Li
arxiv-2407-01640.description: Abstract Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithms are widely used for training deep neural networks but often struggle with slow convergence. To address this issue, we leverage the framework of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and develop a novel data-driven algorithm called batch ADMM (BADM).

arxiv-2410-15025.title: LLM-Driven Learning Analytics Dashboard for Teachers in EFL Writing Education Thanks: Corresponding author.
arxiv-2410-15025.creator: Minsun Kim, SeonGyeom Kim, Suyoun Lee, Yoosang Yoon
arxiv-2410-15025.description: Abstract This paper presents the development of a dashboard designed specifically for teachers in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing education. Leveraging LLMs, the dashboard facilitates the analysis of student interactions with an essay writing system, which integrates ChatGPT for real-time feedback.

arxiv-2504-19391.title: Bi-directional Model Cascading with Proxy Confidence
arxiv-2504-19391.creator: David Warren, Mark Dras
arxiv-2504-19391.description: Abstract Model Cascading, recently applied successfully to LLMs, is a simple but powerful technique that improves the efficiency of inference by selectively applying models of varying sizes. Models are used in sequence from smallest to largest, only deferring samples to large, costly models when smaller models are not sufficiently confident.

pmc-10741044.title: The Influences of Rainfall Intensity and Timing on the Assemblage of Dung Beetles and the Rate of Dung Removal in an Alpine Meadow
pmc-10741044.creator: Wenxiao Sun, Wenting Tang, Yashi Wu, Shuaibing He, Xinwei Wu
pmc-10741044.description: Simple SummaryChanges in precipitation patterns can significantly alter biological processes and associated ecosystem functions. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of rainfall intensity and timing on the structure of dung beetle assemblage and dung mass loss rate in a Tibetan alpine meadow.

pmc-12428415.title: The Role of Doctor Visits, Body Image Discrepancy, and Perceived Health in Predicting Medical Weight Problem Diagnosis
pmc-12428415.creator: Norma Olvera, Rhonda Scherer, Weiwei Wu, Tamal J. Roy, Molly R. Matthews-Ewald, Weihua Fan, Consuelo Arbona
pmc-12428415.description: Background/Objectives: This study investigated how doctor visit(s), body image discrepancy, and perceived health status are associated with receiving a medical weight problem diagnosis. Methods: The sample included 458 Hispanic adults (366 women, 92 men) who completed a health survey at health fairs. Results: Descriptive analyses indicated that 51.4% of women and 54.

pmc-12608024.title: Paradoxical Features Empower Biogenic Silver Nanoparticles
pmc-12608024.creator: Jackeline Pereira, Otto Proaño, Andrea Albán, Marjorie Zambonino, Lynda Mouheb, Morgane Desmau, Ashiqur Rahman, Spiros N. Agathos, Si Amar Dahoumane
pmc-12608024.description: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have drawn great attention, owing to their unique physico-chemical and biological properties and various applications, particularly in the biomedical field. In addition to conventional chemical and physical methods, materials scientists have been exploring the capabilities endowed by several bioresources, such as plants, bacteria, fungi and algae, in the cost-effective and eco-friendly production of AgNPs.

pmc-12617918.title: Understanding EFL learners’ excessive use of translation software: An extension of the flow theory
pmc-12617918.creator: Shuhan Yang
pmc-12617918.description: Grounded in flow theory and the person-artefact-task (PAT) model, this study examines the impact of flow on EFL learners’ excessive use of translation software and identifies the antecedents of flow. This study also investigates whether students’ academic background (English vs. non-English) moderates the relationship between flow and excessive use.

pmc-13010916.title: Transplant-free survival in dengue-associated acute liver failure: Current evidence and future directions
pmc-13010916.creator: Aneel Madhwani, Muhammad Qasim Chaudhry, Jamal Ara Rabbani, Wasila Gul Kakar, Syedda Ayesha, Shahab Abid
pmc-13010916.description: Dengue virus infection is one of the most prevalent arboviral diseases worldwide, particularly affecting tropical and subtropical regions, and continues to pose a significant public health burden. Although hepatic involvement is a well-recognized manifestation of dengue infection, ranging from mild transaminase elevation to severe hepatitis, acute liver failure remains an uncommon but devastating complication associated with exceptionally high mortality.

pmc-13085334.title: How to optimise the use of innovative invasive devices: considerations for feasibility studies
pmc-13085334.creator: Emily Hotton, Julia Wade, Daisy Elliott, Erik Lenguerrand, Joanna Crofts, Natalie Blencowe
pmc-13085334.description: Innovation in medical devices is essential for advancing patient care but has been undermined by inadequate evaluation and regulation. The UK vaginal mesh scandal exposed systemic flaws in medical device evaluation, where insufficient pre-market testing and ineffective post-market surveillance caused harm to countless women. Unlike pharmaceutical products, medical devices often enter clinical practice without robust evidence or long-term safety data.

pmc-13195800.title: Diagnostic dilemma between probable cardiac sarcoidosis and non-granulomatous myocarditis: a grand round case report
pmc-13195800.creator: Tulluru Ravi Sankar, M Ananthakrishna, A Arpudh Michael, P Sirish Chandra Srinath, T Viji Samuel
pmc-13195800.description: BackgroundCardiac sarcoidosis (CS) can mimic other inflammatory cardiomyopathies, and true steroid resistance is uncommon. Distinguishing granulomatous myocardial involvement from active non-granulomatous myocarditis remains clinically challenging.Case summaryA 43-year-old woman with biopsy-proven systemic sarcoidosis and dilated cardiomyopathy presented with recurrent decompensated heart failure (HF). Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography–computed tomography demonstrated diffuse myocardial uptake and was interpreted as probable CS.

pmc-13266003.title: Effect of spraying Bacillus coagulans during incubation on hatchability, chick growth, resistance to Mycoplasma synoviae, and cecal microbiota
pmc-13266003.creator: Yimin Wei, Xuli Zhao, Xing Chen, Xiaomeng Miao, Wen Li, Ying Ma, Xiaoyu Zhao, Zhonghua Ning
pmc-13266003.description: Mycoplasma synoviae (MS) causes synovitis and airsacculitis in laying hens, reducing production performance and resulting in economic losses. Leveraging the acid-intolerant nature of MS, this study sprayed acid-producing Bacillus coagulans (B. coagulans) during incubation, investigating the effects on hatchability, chick growth, resistance to MS, and cecal microbiota.

pmc-13381375.title: The benefit of using dynamic rather than static heat assessment methods early in a mine water energy project
pmc-13381375.creator: Alexandra Sweeney, Jeroen van Hunen, Julien Mouli-Castillo, Jon Gluyas
pmc-13381375.description: Mine water geothermal (MWG) heating offers a low-carbon solution for space heating, helping to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. To assess the feasibility of an MWG scheme, an estimate of extractable heat is required to size the system, to determine if it meets surface demand, and evaluate economic viability.
